label: Radicalized Mencian moral intuition into the universal innate knowing (liangzhi) of Mind
description: Wang Yangming revived Mencius’s concept of liangzhi (innate moral knowing) as the immediate, self-authenticating moral compass present in every human being.
dialecticalTension: Democratizes sagehood by locating ultimate moral authority inside ordinary human conscience.

label: Shared Chan/Zen emphasis on immediate mind-awakening and non-duality of practice and realization
description: Critics and scholars alike note how Wang Yangming’s Xinxue absorbed Chan Buddhist immediacy of mind while insisting on Confucian social engagement.
dialecticalTension: Echoes Zen practice-realization non-duality within Neo-Confucian civic ethics.

label: Formulated Zhixing Heyi: genuine moral knowing is already enacted in ethical conduct
description: Wang Yangming dissolved the gap between theoretical cognition and moral praxis, arguing that knowing filiality or justice without acting is not yet genuine knowledge.
dialecticalTension: Overcomes epistemic-practical dualism in classical ethical psychology.

label: Informed modern Japanese philosophical emphasis on pure experience and active intuition
description: Wang Yangming’s philosophy of Mind (Yomeigaku) deeply shaped Meiji and Taisho thinkers, resonating in Nishida’s unified "pure experience."
dialecticalTension: Bridges Ming Xinxue to modern Kyoto School phenomenology of action.
